result:
Nothing in `ces-revisions` produces a result yet. `main()` prints a greeting, and no roadmap or spec exists. So this goes through New-Project Entry. I'm treating `specs/ces-revisions-prompt.md` as your own words for what you want. The three research files are background: they supply facts, options and costs, but no outcomes. Parts A and B of the brief (the literature review and the gap analysis) are already delivered by those files, so they aren't outcomes here.

**Outcome candidates (unranked, from `specs/ces-revisions-prompt.md`)**

| # | Outcome | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|
| O1 | Revision-scale history for total nonfarm: dispersion (MAR, tail quantiles) of each of the four revision stages over time, with 2003 and 2020–22 marked | Small data, likely MBs. ALFRED API limit is 120 requests/min. Real vintage depth is measured by the work |
| O2 | The same history by NAICS supersector, NSA and SA | Supersectors × 2 adjustments × vintages. Volume is measured by the work |
| O3 | Split of one- and two-month SA revisions into an NSA-sample component and a seasonal-factor component (Part C, seasonality; the research files say no published long-run version exists) | Needs NSA and SA vintages together. Cost unknown until run |
| O4 | Estimated effect of collection interval and first-closing rate on one-month revision scale | Collection days are derivable from release calendars. Closing rates are published only for recent years, and archive depth is unknown until run |
| O5 | Benchmark revision scale per year (preliminary and final), its sector spread, and the wedge-back pattern on the months in between | About 20+ benchmark articles to collect. Partner/agent hours are unknown until run |
| O6 | Annual operational-capacity covariates (real appropriations, FTE, sample size, shutdowns/CRs/sequestration), each value traced to its source | Hand-built from budget justifications and FedScope over roughly 40 years. This is mostly partner time, measured by the work |
| O7 | Descriptive (explicitly non-causal) estimates of how capacity covariates relate to revision scale, under horseshoe shrinkage | Depends on O6 |
| O8 | The full Bayesian multi-vintage model (Part C): latent path, stage-specific news/noise, Student-t with SV and covariates in log-scale, benchmark as an irregular observation, supersector pooling, validated by PPC, LOO against constant variance, and pseudo-real-time checks | NUTS cost is unknown until a fit runs. A one-fit timing probe on O1 data is available on your yes |

Qualities to place when the roadmap is written: manifests, traceability, point-in-time awareness, full validation suites.

**Proposed tracks**

- **A — Revision-scale history (O1, O2): known progression**, provided you can name its steps end to end. If you can't, it becomes research.
- **B — Seasonal vs sample (O3): research.** It is split from A and C because the decomposition stands whether or not collection timing matters.
- **C — Collection interval (O4): research.** It is split from B for the same reason in reverse. It is a within-year question, unrelated to slow-moving capacity.
- **D — Benchmark and wedge-back (O5): research.** Its source data (benchmark articles) and revision stage are distinct from the monthly sample revisions.
- **E — Operational capacity (O6, O7): research.** It is split off so that O1–O5 don't wait on hand-building budget series. Its answer is descriptive either way.
- **F — Joint model (O8): research.** Joined to the others, every answer would wait on the full state-space machinery. It reuses their data, but it doesn't gate them.

**Choices already made**
- Python 3.14 (`.python-version`), managed with uv, tested with pytest, linted with ruff.
- NumPyro/NUTS, Dynamax, Blackjax (only if warranted), ArviZ, Polars (from the brief).
- Estimand: revision scale, so covariates enter the variance or scale, not only the mean (from the brief).

**Proposed roadmap name:** `ces-revisions`, which gives `specs/ces-revisions-roadmap.md`. That file does not exist yet.

**Please:** rank the outcomes within each track, rank the tracks against each other, and confirm or change the tracks, their kinds and the name. If you also want the NUTS timing probe or a one-series ALFRED vintage fetch to firm up the cost notes, say so in the same reply.
